questions.stem_text: The Mayan king Yax Pahsaj symbolized his royalty on a stele that depicts:

options.A: a series of decisive military conquests against a rival king.
options.B: a depiction of him as a corn god, a symbol of fertility and prosperity.
options.C: a scene of him hunting and defeating a large jaguar.
options.D: an eagle, a serpent, and a jaguar, all of which were important royal animals.
options.E: him receiving a crown from the Mayan god of death and rebirth.

questions.answer_explanation: The depiction of a series of decisive military conquests against a rival king on the stele symbolizes Yax Pahsaj's authority and legitimacy as a ruler in Mayan society, reflecting the importance of military success in establishing and maintaining royal power.

questions.stem_text:
In primates, the location of which of the following determines if it is a quadruped or
biped?
questions.answer_explanation: The foramen magnum's position at the base of the skull indicates whether the spine connects vertically (bipedalism) or horizontally (quadrupedalism) to the skull, thus determining the locomotion type in primates.
